Revenue came in a little light because of gas deflation, and the executive's comments about cutting prices on several items implied less pricing power. Expectations for near-term revenue growth and margins were trimmed.

label: outlier
cause: The stock fell 4.3% on 2024-07-11 despite a positive-looking announcement. Costco raised US and Canada membership fees by about 8% (to $65 and $130) effective Sept. 1, its first hike since 2017, and reported June sales up 7.4%. Fee income is a high-margin source of profit, so the hike should lift operating margins and earnings visibility into 2026. However, the hike had been widely anticipated and the shares had run up, so the move looks like a sell-the-news reaction, with the already-priced-in fee increase and sales failing to add new upside. The statements do not explicitly confirm this reasoning, which makes the cause uncertain.
expected_before_vs_after: Before: the market already expected a fee hike was due after seven years, and the stock had priced much of the earnings benefit in. After: the hike came as expected (about 8%, effective Sept. 1) with solid June sales, so there was little new upside surprise, and the shares fell.
